title: Python Programming Fundamentals
subtitle: Write clear, tested Python programs from the first line of code
audience_line: Beginners, students and professionals learning to program with Python
overview: This programme teaches participants to program in Python from the very beginning. They set up a working environment, then learn variables and types, conditions and loops, lists, dictionaries and other data structures, functions, modules and packages, virtual environments and their first unit tests with pytest. They read and write files, handle errors, work with JSON and CSV data, and organise code with classes and dataclasses. Every chapter ends with exercises at the keyboard, and the programme closes with a final project in which each participant builds, tests and presents a command-line application.

facts.label: Audience
facts.value: Beginners, students and professionals learning to program with Python

facts.label: Prerequisites
facts.value: None. Basic computer use; no programming experience needed

facts.label: Duration
facts.value: 27 h: 24 h of chapters + 3 h buffer

facts.label: Format
facts.value: Short lectures with live coding, each followed by guided exercises

facts.label: Lab environment
facts.value: Runs locally: one laptop per participant with Python 3, VS Code and Git, installed in the first chapter; no account or cost

facts.label: Assessment
facts.value: Exercises validated at the end of each phase and a final project presented to the group; certificate of completion for participants who complete both

facts.label: Outcome
facts.value: Participants can write, organise and test Python programs that use data structures, functions, files, error handling and classes

phases.name: Python Basics
phases.focus: Setup, variables, types, operators, input and output, conditions and loops
phases.intro: Participants install Python and VS Code, write their first programs with variables, types, operators and input and output, then control the flow of a program with conditions and loops. Validated exercise: a number-guessing game that checks each guess is within range and counts the attempts.

chapters.title: Getting Started
chapters.content: Setup, variables, types, operators, input and output

phases.name: Data Structures & Functions
phases.focus: Lists, tuples, dictionaries, sets, comprehensions, functions, modules, pytest
phases.intro: Participants store and transform data with lists, tuples, dictionaries, sets and comprehensions, then split their code into functions, modules and packages, manage dependencies with venv and pip, and write their first unit tests with pytest. Validated exercise: a module of text-statistics functions with passing pytest tests.

chapters.title: Functions & Modules
chapters.content: Functions, scope, modules, packages, venv and pip, first unit tests with pytest

phases.name: Files, Errors & Objects
phases.focus: File input and output, exceptions, JSON and CSV, classes, inheritance, dataclasses
phases.intro: Participants read and write files, handle errors with exceptions, exchange data as JSON and CSV, then model their programs with classes, inheritance and dataclasses. Validated exercise: a contact book stored in a JSON file, with classes for its entries and graceful handling of a missing or corrupted file.

chapters.title: Files & Errors
chapters.content: File input and output, exceptions, JSON and CSV

phases.name: Final Project
phases.focus: A tested command-line application, presented to the group
phases.intro: Each participant builds a command-line application from a short brief, such as a task manager or an expense tracker, reusing the exercises of the phases, then presents it to the group.

chapters.title: Brief & Build
chapters.content: Choose the brief, design the modules and classes, write the application with file storage, command-line arguments with argparse

chapters.title: Test & Document
chapters.content: pytest tests for the main functions, error handling, README

chapters.title: Demo & Review
chapters.content: Live demo and code walkthrough; questions and feedback

project.title: Command-Line Application
project.brief: A command-line application, such as a task manager or an expense tracker, organised in modules and classes, storing its data in files, handling errors and covered by pytest tests.
project.stack: Python 3, standard library (json, csv, argparse, dataclasses), pytest, Git, VS Code
project.deliverable: Git repository with code, tests and README, live demo
